notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked; simulated R0; model-authored and unreviewed, with reviewed_by null and no human review or test claimed; no hardware run and no MHS-Device level claimed). The package binds the privileged TacEx ball-rolling task (TacEx-Ball-Rolling-Privileged-v0) through the Gymnasium family bridge and serves cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. NOT COVERED: the TacEx vision and tactile observation arrays (tactile RGB images, depth, Taxim-FOTS marker motion, UIPC soft bodies); this package binds the privileged 14-value scalar observation instead, which the cap.world.* classes can carry, and the other entry symbol of the card (BallRollingTactileRGBEnv) is not bound. The upstream stack (Isaac Sim 4.5, Isaac Lab 2.1.1, Linux, an NVIDIA GPU) was never started here, so the sim backend was not run; upstream tasks are constructed with gym.make(task_name, cfg=env_cfg) and the cfg cannot be built without that stack. The fake is an F0 kinematic stand-in: no Isaac Sim physics, contacts, friction, mass, IK, Franka arm, tactile/RGB/depth sensor, rendering or noise model; the ball follows the end effector; only the success reward term is modelled; the end-effector pose, push gain and contact radius are placeholders; the truncation is the fake's floor(episode_length_s / dt) = 416 (the source comment says 500; the rounding lives in Isaac Lab's external DirectRLEnv and was not run); the 1024-environment vectorization is reduced to one environment; and the goal RNG differs from Isaac Lab's sample_uniform, so one seed does not give the same goal on both. These reductions are in fidelity.gaps. The action bound [-1, 1] is the clamp at base_env.py:381; the fake's five-element action Box uses it, so the bridge publishes action.values and G6 exercises the envelope. Warnings are explained: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 is expected because the seed only sets the next reset, as in the Gymnasium exemplar; G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space, reset and step is expected because BallRollingEnv inherits them from Isaac Lab's DirectRLEnv outside the clone; the four G8.NO_UNIT warnings are the bridge-derived integer and action inputs. There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No catalogue requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used. The upstream licence is pinned as the card says (NOASSERTION, license_class unknown); the README shows an MIT badge but the clone has no licence file, so no other licence is claimed. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
